problem:
Consider the curve defined parametrically as 

$$
x=3{t}^{2},\,y=2{t}^{3},\,t\in [0,\sqrt{3}].
$$

Calculate the surface area generated when this curve is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $y$-axis.
worked_solution:
We can find the surface area generated when a curve is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $y$-axis using the formula

$$
S=\int 2\pi x\,\text{d}s.
$$

Since our curve is given in parametric form, we have

$$
\text{d}s=\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t.
$$

Therefore, we will use

$$
S=2\pi {\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}x\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t.
$$

We are told that the limits of integration are from ${t}_{1}=0$ to ${t}_{2}=\sqrt{3}.$ 

Computing the derivatives, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{2})=6t \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{3})=6{t}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}S & =2\pi {\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}x\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{3}}3{t}^{2}\sqrt{{(6t)}^{2}+{(6{t}^{2})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{3}}3{t}^{2}\sqrt{36{t}^{2}+36{t}^{4}}\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}
$$

Now, factoring the expression $36{t}^{2}+36{t}^{4},$ we can rewrite our integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}S & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{3}}3{t}^{2}\sqrt{36{t}^{2}+36{t}^{4}}\,\text{d}t] \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{3}}3{t}^{2}\sqrt{36{t}^{2}(1+{t}^{2})}\,\text{d}t \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{3}}3{t}^{2}\cdot |6t|\sqrt{1+{t}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{3}}3{t}^{2}\cdot 6t\sqrt{1+{t}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & =18\pi {\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{3}}2{t}^{3}\sqrt{1+{t}^{2}}\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}
$$

We evaluate the last integral using the substitution $u=1+{t}^{2}$ Then, ${t}^{2}=u-1$ and $\text{d}u=2t\,\text{d}t.$ We also need to compute new limits, given below.

| **$t$** | $0$ | $\sqrt{3}$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $1$ | $4$ |

Therefore, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}S & =18\pi {\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{3}}2{t}^{3}\sqrt{1+{t}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & =18\pi {\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{3}}2t\cdot {t}^{2}\sqrt{1+{t}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & =18\pi {\int }_{1}^{4}(u-1)\sqrt{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =18\pi {\int }_{1}^{4}(u-1){u}^{1/2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =18\pi {\int }_{1}^{4}({u}^{3/2}-{u}^{1/2})\,\text{d}u \\  & =18\pi \cdot {[\frac{2{u}^{5/2}}{5}-\frac{2{u}^{3/2}}{3}]}_{1}^{4} \\  & =18\pi [(\frac{2({4}^{5/2})}{5}-\frac{2({4}^{3/2})}{3})-(\frac{2}{5}-\frac{2}{3})] \\  & =18\pi \cdot [(\frac{64}{5}-\frac{16}{3})-(\frac{2}{5}-\frac{2}{3})) \\  & =18\pi \cdot (\frac{62}{5}-\frac{14}{3}) \\  & =18\pi \cdot \frac{116}{15} \\  & =\frac{696\pi }{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
